# Morphiqo

> Morphiqo swaps faces in videos and photos entirely on the user's own device.
> Nothing is uploaded: there is no server, no account and no copy of the user's
> media anywhere but their own hardware.

Morphiqo ships as three implementations of one pipeline — a web app that runs in
the browser, an iOS app, and a macOS app — and they are meant to produce the same
result from the same inputs.

## How it works

- Face detection, identity encoding, swapping and optional enhancement all run
  locally, using the device's own CPU, GPU or Neural Engine.
- The AI models are too large to ship inside the app, so on first launch it
  downloads roughly 900 MB once, over HTTPS, from the public releases of the
  open-source FaceFusion project. Every byte is checked against a SHA-256 digest.
- After that download, the iOS and macOS apps work with the network switched off
  entirely. The web version needs the network only to load the page.

## Requirements

- Web: Chrome or Edge 121+, Safari 17+, or a recent Chrome on Android. Needs Web
  Workers, WebCodecs, OffscreenCanvas and the Origin Private File System. There
  is no server-side fallback.
- iOS: iOS 17 or later.
- macOS: macOS 14 or later, Apple silicon or Intel.

## Privacy

- No accounts, no advertising, no crash-reporting SDK.
- Photos and videos are never transmitted. Face embeddings are computed on the
  device, held in memory for the current job only, and discarded — they are never
  stored, never profiled and never compared against any database of people.
- The website counts page views in aggregate, cookielessly. The iOS and macOS
  apps contain no analytics of any kind.

## Responsible use

The face-swapping models are published for non-commercial research use. Only
swap faces of people who have agreed to it.
